title: Laser Guide Star in Paranal
caption: The Laser Guide Star Facility under the southern sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars fill this night sky over Paranal Observatory, but other objects stand out too. At the bottom left is the pinkish Carina Nebula. Higher up shines a bright bluish star, Canopus, the second-brightest star in the night sky. To the right of Canopus are two bluish clouds: the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, irregular galaxies that neighbour the Milky Way.

To study such objects in more detail, ground-based telescopes must overcome the turbulence of Earth's atmosphere, which blurs astronomical images. The Very Large Telescope tackles this with adaptive optics, helped by lasers fired from the Laser Guide Star Facility on Unit Telescope 4.

The lasers excite sodium atoms high in the atmosphere, which then give off light. That light is disturbed by moving air in the same way as starlight. By collecting it, the adaptive optics system can measure the atmosphere's distortions and correct for them.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Carina Nebula's pink colour and the Magellanic Clouds appear more vivid than they would to an observer.
